rationale:
SPLIT into two independent children. Each is a genuine, reusable obligation of the supplied proof, and each is already a comparator-accepted DAG theorem with a byte-identical frozen Lean type. The controller therefore maps each child onto the existing accepted node instead of proving it again.

Structure of the supplied proof:
- Step 1 compares norms: |φ| ≤ √(Pⁿ)‖φ‖, followed by the separate remark √(Pⁿ) ≤ Pⁿ. This is a pure linear-algebra fact about covectors and becomes child `covector_norm_le_opnorm`, Lean name `fiw_ims_sc_covectorNorm_le_opNorm`. It is accepted at DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.series_current-a1.covector_norm-a1, candidate c8cb71851ed3018dcc8a0a89a946b8610884f81a.
- Steps 2–4 (homogeneity, admissibility of ±ω/s, the le_massOn supremum bound, then s = K₀ or s ↓ 0) use only one fact about ω: a pointwise coefficient-norm bound K₀. With K₀ replaced by an arbitrary bound C, these steps are exactly child `coeff_norm_mass_bound`, Lean name `cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le`. It is accepted at root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.mass_bound-a1, candidate ba202ac0407b6e93210594416fcd0729874b2eff. About 15 other decompositions already share it with the same type.

How the children imply the selected statement. Assume 0 ≤ B, M_W(T) ≤ ofReal B, tsupport ω ⊆ W, and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x.
(i) C ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0.
(ii) k := Pⁿ is a natural number. If k = 0 then √0 = 0 ≤ 0. If k ≥ 1 then k ≤ k², so √k ≤ k (Real.sqrt_le_iff). This is the parent's "√k ≤ k" remark.
(iii) For every x, child covector_norm_le_opnorm gives |ω(x)| ≤ √(Pⁿ)‖ω(x)‖. Since √(Pⁿ) ≥ 0, this is ≤ √(Pⁿ)·C, and since C ≥ 0 and √(Pⁿ) ≤ Pⁿ, it is ≤ Pⁿ·C. This is the parent's Step 1 conclusion.
(iv) Apply child coeff_norm_mass_bound with C' := Pⁿ·C = K₀, which is the parent's Steps 2–4. It gives |T(ω)| ≤ B·(Pⁿ·C) = Pⁿ·B·C by ring.
The children are independent (no sibling dependencies), so the dependency graph is acyclic.

Public source: L. Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5 (definition of mass) and Remark 2.6 (Euclidean coefficient norm). The child proofs below are extracted from the supplied parent proof (Step 1, and Steps 2–4), with the missing details filled in.

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector is at most √(Pⁿ) times its operator norm (Simon 6, Remark 2.6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P, i.e. α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ. Let ‖α‖ be its operator norm with respect to the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P. Let |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} a_I)^{1/2}, where e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k is the k-th standard basis vector, a_I := α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² if I is strictly increasing, and a_I := 0 otherwise. Then |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖, where Pⁿ is the real number (P : ℝ)ⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ Real.sqrt ((P : ℝ) ^ n) * ‖α‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (comparison of norms; Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.6), for an arbitrary n-covector α, stopped at the bound √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖. The parent applies the further remark √(Pⁿ) ≤ Pⁿ itself.

Notation. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k. For I : Fin n → Fin P let e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n. Let a_I := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and a_I := 0 otherwise. By definition, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} a_I). Pⁿ denotes the real number (P : ℝ)ⁿ, which is the cast of the natural number Pⁿ.

1. Unit vectors. EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_k‖ = 1 for every k ∈ Fin P (OrthonormalBasis.norm_eq_one).

2. Each coefficient is bounded by the operator norm. Fix I : Fin n → Fin P. The operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives ‖α(e_I)‖ ≤ ‖α‖·Π_{i : Fin n} ‖e_{I(i)}‖. By Step 1 every factor of the product equals 1, so the product equals 1; this includes n = 0, where the product is empty. The norm on ℝ is the absolute value, so |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖.

3. Each summand is at most ‖α‖². Let I : Fin n → Fin P. If I is strictly increasing, then a_I = α(e_I)² = |α(e_I)|² ≤ ‖α‖², because 0 ≤ |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖ by Step 2 and t ↦ t² is monotone on [0, ∞). Otherwise a_I = 0 ≤ ‖α‖².

4. Counting. The finite type of all maps Fin n → Fin P has exactly Pⁿ elements (Fintype.card_fun, with card(Fin n) = n and card(Fin P) = P). Summing Step 3 over all I gives Σ_I a_I ≤ Σ_I ‖α‖² = Pⁿ·‖α‖². If P = 0 and n ≥ 1 the index type is empty and both sides are 0, so the inequality still holds.

5. Taking square roots. The square root is monotone on ℝ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt), so |α| = √(Σ_I a_I) ≤ √(Pⁿ·‖α‖²). Since Pⁿ ≥ 0, √(Pⁿ·‖α‖²) = √(Pⁿ)·√(‖α‖²) (Real.sqrt_mul). Since ‖α‖ ≥ 0, √(‖α‖²) = ‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_sq). Hence covectorEuclideanNorm α = |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖e_k‖ = 1 for the standard orthonormal basis e_k = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k.
ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖α‖ for every I : Fin n → Fin P.
Every summand a_I of |α|² is ≤ ‖α‖²: it is α(e_I)² ≤ ‖α‖² when I is strictly increasing, and 0 otherwise.
There are Pⁿ maps Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I a_I ≤ Pⁿ·‖α‖².
Monotonicity and multiplicativity of √, with √(‖α‖²) = ‖α‖, give |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖.

subproblems.title: Mass bound for test forms with bounded Euclidean coefficient norm (Simon 6, 2.4–2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n), and B, C ∈ ℝ. Assume 0 ≤ B, M_W(T) ≤ B (that is, T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B), tsupport ω ⊆ W, and |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors on ℝ^P (Simon 6, Remark 2.6). Then |T(ω)| ≤ B·C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2–4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5: M_W(T) is the supremum of T over test forms supported in W with Euclidean coefficient norm at most 1), with the coefficient bound K₀ = Pⁿ·C replaced by the given bound C.

Notation. For an n-covector φ on ℝ^P, |φ| := covectorEuclideanNorm φ = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} a_I(φ)), where a_I(φ) := φ(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and a_I(φ) := 0 otherwise. Here e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) and e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k.

1. Homogeneity. Let t ∈ ℝ and let φ be an n-covector. Since (tφ)(e_I) = t·φ(e_I), we have a_I(tφ) = t²·a_I(φ) for every I; both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence |tφ| = √(t²·Σ_I a_I(φ)) = √(t²)·√(Σ_I a_I(φ)) = |t|·|φ|, by Real.sqrt_mul (t² ≥ 0) and √(t²) = |t| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

2. C ≥ 0. The point 0 ∈ ℝ^P exists, |ω(0)| ≥ 0 because it is a square root (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), and |ω(0)| ≤ C by hypothesis. Hence C ≥ 0.

3. Rescaled forms are admissible. Let s > 0 with s ≥ C, let ε ∈ {1, −1}, and put t := ε/s, so that |t| = 1/s.
- The form η := t·ω belongs to Dⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n, because TestFormOn U n is a real submodule of DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n. As a function, η(x) = t·ω(x).
- Its topological support satisfies tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, by tsupport_smul_subset_right and the hypothesis.
- For every x, Step 1, the hypothesis |ω(x)| ≤ C and C ≤ s give |η(x)| = |t|·|ω(x)| = s⁻¹·|ω(x)| ≤ s⁻¹·C ≤ s⁻¹·s = 1.
Hence η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, whose two defining conditions are tsupport η ⊆ W and |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.

4. Mass inequality. By definition, M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(η')) over η' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Therefore ENNReal.ofReal(T(η)) ≤ M_W(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B). Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal(p) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B) implies p ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), so T(η) ≤ B. The current T is linear on TestFormOn U n, so T(η) = t·T(ω) = (ε/s)·T(ω). Multiplying (ε/s)·T(ω) ≤ B by s > 0 gives ε·T(ω) ≤ s·B.

5. Absolute value. Step 4 with ε = 1 gives T(ω) ≤ s·B, and with ε = −1 gives −T(ω) ≤ s·B. Therefore |T(ω)| ≤ s·B for every real s > 0 with s ≥ C.

6. Conclusion. By Step 2, either C > 0 or C = 0.
- If C > 0, take s := C in Step 5: |T(ω)| ≤ C·B = B·C.
- If C = 0, Step 5 gives |T(ω)| ≤ s·B for every s > 0. Suppose |T(ω)| > 0, and take s := |T(ω)|/(B + 1), which is > 0 because B + 1 > 0. Then |T(ω)| ≤ s·B = |T(ω)|·B/(B + 1) < |T(ω)|, because B/(B + 1) < 1. This is a contradiction, so |T(ω)| ≤ 0 = B·C.
In both cases |T(ω)| ≤ B·C. ∎
proof_key_steps: For s > 0 with s ≥ C and ε = ±1, the form (ε/s)·ω is in TestFormOn U n, has tsupport ⊆ W and coefficient norm ≤ 1, so it lies in massAdmissibleOn U n W.
GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, M_W(T) ≤ ofReal B and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (B ≥ 0) give (ε/s)·T(ω) ≤ B, hence ε·T(ω) ≤ s·B by linearity of T.
Both signs give |T(ω)| ≤ s·B for every s > 0 with s ≥ C.
Take s = C if C > 0. If C = 0, choosing s = |T(ω)|/(B+1) rules out |T(ω)| > 0, so |T(ω)| ≤ 0 = B·C.
